The `NumericEntityUnescaper` class has a `translate` method that processes character entities in the input string. The method checks for numeric entities starting with `&#` and translates them to the corresponding characters.

Based on the failing test `org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaperTest.testUnfinishedEntity()`, it seems that the test is trying to unescape the string `"Test &#x30 not test"`. The expected unescaped string is `"Test \u0030 not test"`.

The current bug report describes a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when calling `unescapeHtml4` on the string `"&#03"`. This exception occurs in the `translate` method of `NumericEntityUnescaper` at line 49, where it appears that the index used to access characters in the input string is going out of bounds.

By examining the `translate` method of `NumericEntityUnescaper`, the issue may be related to how the method handles the extraction of the numeric entity value from the input string. If the method incorrectly calculates the end index of the entity value or accesses characters beyond the string length, it could result in a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

To further diagnose the issue and locate the exact source of the problem, we should carefully review the logic for extracting and parsing the numeric entity value in the `translate` method of `NumericEntityUnescaper`.
The issue likely occurs in the method responsible for extracting and parsing the numeric entity value in the `NumericEntityUnescaper` class. To fix this issue, the following method should be updated:

```java
org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaper.translate(java.lang.CharSequence,int,java.io.Writer)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
